subject: Discovery recap + POC scope (function calls & structured outputs)
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Kate Dawson <kate.dawson@acme-payments.com>, Miguel Ortiz <miguel.ortiz@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap + POC scope (function calls & structured outputs)

Kate / Miguel — thanks again for a productive call this morning. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, suggested technical approach, and concrete next steps so we can get a scoped POC moving next week. Please flag anything that looks off.

What you told us (pain & context)
- Pain: inconsistent downstream parsing of LLM responses for payments routing (free-form reply text leads to engineering fragility).
- Pain: current post-processing (regex + heuristics in Node microservice) is brittle and hard to scale across new use cases.
- Current stack: OpenAI-hosted models (gpt-4.family) via a gateway, Node-based orchestration, internal event bus, on-prem PCI-controlled DB for certain fields.
- Constraints: data residency for payment IDs, strict audit trail, and SLO on response time (~<400ms for the critical routing path).

What success looks like (your criteria)
- Deterministic structured output that validates against JSON schema (fields always present when applicable).
- >=95% of responses are parseable without fallback pipeline work.
- Latency within target for 95th percentile (<400ms) for live traffic.
- Clear audit logs for every inference (model, inputs, tokens).

Suggested approach for the POC (high level)
1) Enforce schema via function-calling / structured output (server-side validation).
2) Provide a strict reference JSON schema (we'll share an example file) and a validator in the POC harness.
3) Use low temperature/top_p settings and prompt engineering to avoid “assistant commentary”.
4) Implement a small agent workflow: inference -> schema validator -> reranker/repair step (if invalid) -> fallback to human review after N failures.
5) Instrument with token and latency tracing so we can optimize batching and model variant selection.

Immediate next steps (owners & timing)
- Hannah: Share example JSON schema and Redwood POC outline (attached). Delivery by EOD today.
- Karthik: Technical deep-dive (45m) to scope integration points, host/region, and security controls. Proposed slots below.
- Acme: Confirm procurement contact and NDA status so we can circulate the SOW.

Attachments: example_schema.json (sample expected output), redwood-poc-outline.pdf (recommended scope & milestones).

Thanks — looking forward to the technical session.

— Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0143

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Kate Dawson <kate.dawson@acme-payments.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Feb 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + POC scope (function calls & structured outputs)

Adding a couple technical clarifications we should include in the POC scope:

- Model / response control:
  * Use function_call or Redwood's structured-output enforcement so the LLM returns a single JSON payload (no freeform preface/suffix).
  * Set temperature=0.0–0.2 and deterministic decoding (beam/greedy) for the POC to maximize parseability.

- Schema & failure modes:
  * Schema must allow an error envelope: {"status":"ok|error","payload":{...},"error_code":null, "diagnostics":{}}
  * Define repair policy: 1 auto-repair attempt via constrained prompt -> 2nd attempt triggers a reranker service that tries a smaller template model -> if still invalid, escalate to human review.

- Agent workflow notes:
  * Tool/Function bindings: payment-lookup (internal webhook), risk-check (sync call to internal service), emit-event (to event bus).
  * Prefer a two-stage run: inference (structured output) then side-effects only after schema validation and rate-limited writes to PCI DB.

- Observability success criteria:
  * 95% parseable at P0, error-rate <5% on production-like traffic; per-route token and latency histograms retained for 30 days.

I'll bring a minimal demo of the validator + retry logic to the deep-dive so we can align on exact interfaces.

— Karthik
Head of Solutions Architecture (Redwood)

Thanks Hannah & Karthik — this captures the discussion well. Two quick asks from our side before we book the deep-dive:

1) Procurement / NDA: please send NDA and SOW routing info to procurement@acme-payments.com. We typically need a standard mutual NDA before sharing sample production data.
2) Residency: for the POC, we need assurances that any tokenized payment identifiers used during testing are treated per our PCI rules and not persisted in third-party logs. Can you include a short note in the SOW about logging controls?

If you can get the NDA and outline in place, we can lock the deep-dive for next week.

Best,
Kate
